headline: Sub-Cent Gas Fees for Real-Time Blockchain Games on Base
summary: Discover how Base's Layer 2 solution enables seamless, low-cost transactions, unlocking new possibilities for on-chain gaming experiences.
details: High gas fees and slow transaction times have been major hurdles for blockchain gaming, preventing the fluid, real-time interactions players expect. To address this, the developer of yoss.gg, a zero-rake P2P USDC coin flip game, turned to Base, Coinbase's Layer 2 solution on Ethereum.

Base offers sub-cent gas fees and high throughput, making it ideal for frequent transactions. This technical overview explores how Base achieves these low costs through optimistic rollups, which bundle transactions off-chain and submit proofs to Ethereum's mainnet, drastically reducing per-transaction expenses.

The platform's support for the EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) means developers can easily adapt existing Solidity smart contracts. Additionally, Base benefits from Coinbase's robust infrastructure and user onboarding capabilities, streamlining the development and deployment process.

By leveraging Base, games like yoss.gg can offer instant and cheap settlements using stablecoins, providing a user experience comparable to traditional games. This is a significant step towards mainstream adoption of blockchain gaming.

If you're building games that require frequent on-chain interactions, Base presents a compelling platform. Its ability to deliver fast, cheap transactions unlocks gameplay patterns that were previously too expensive on Ethereum mainnet, paving the way for more engaging decentralized experiences.

headline: Nvidia & SK Group form $500B AI partnership to build massive AI infrastructure
summary: The two tech giants are teaming up to supercharge AI infrastructure with next-gen memory and AI factories, with the first data center set to go live in 2027.
details: Nvidia and SK Group have signed letters of intent for a strategic relationship valued at over $500 billion. This collaboration spans a long-term memory supply agreement with SK hynix and plans for SK Telecom to build a 2-gigawatt AI data center in South Korea.

The new AI data center, slated to begin service in 2027, will utilize Nvidia's DSX AI factory platform and feature Vera Rubin accelerated computing systems equipped with SK hynix HBM4 memory. This infrastructure aims to support sovereign, enterprise, physical, and agentic AI deployments across the Asia-Pacific region.

The $500 billion valuation represents the aggregate commercial activity expected between Nvidia and SK Group over several years. It encompasses AI infrastructure construction and a significant long-term memory supply agreement, consolidating these efforts under one strategic umbrella.

While specific hardware details remain vague, the 2 GW AI data center is anticipated to house thousands of NVL72 VR200 racks and hundreds of thousands of AI accelerators. Nvidia's DSX platform is designed for data center-scale AI, focusing on low-cost token generation and energy efficiency.
